summary: First end-to-end test of the Safety Gate plus an independent mobile accessibility check. BACKEND: test_safety_gate.py passes 21/21. A new external-URL suite (test_safety_gate_external.py) passes 13/13. It covers points 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 11, openapi hiding, support seeing safety_mode only, and the admin export and daily counts (403 for a parent, 401 or 403 when signed out, 200 for admin, no-store, counts go up by applied +2 / ignored +1 / downloads +1, no case IDs). The old /api/safety-assessment questions, POST and /me all return 404, so the old check-in is off. FRONTEND (390x844 and 1920x800, two fresh linked parents): both parents get the same banner text, the link opens /case-settings with neutral wording, and after a signed webhook (professional + parallel_parenting) both see 'Some features are set by your professional for this case.' plus plan-options-card -> /plan-options with only parallel options and no toast or dialog. The banner shows in the Communication Builder and the BIFF coach drawer. /help works signed in and signed out with all required content. Quick exit -> /calendar, and Back does not return to /help. /safety-assessment -> /help. Admin export downloads and the daily counts table goes up by 1 download with no overflow at 390. Help-services add, edit and delete work. A parent is denied on both admin pages. FAILURES: (1) turning on Grey-rock in the BIFF drawer shows safety and coercion wording and 'Advocate' labels; (2) several accessibility failures, listed below.

minor.issue: Not a code bug. The external ingress rewrites Cache-Control to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate'. no-store is still there. Tests should check that no-store is included, not that the header equals it.

ui_bugs.component: BiffTab (shown when the GreyRockToggleChip is on)
ui_bugs.issue: Turning Grey-rock on by hand shows wording that gives a reason, which breaks the 'plain toggle, no reason, no safety-check wording' rule. biff-greyrock-chip title='Because your Quick Safety Check flagged coercion or safety concerns, the coach is producing shorter, more neutral replies.'. The subtitle says 'Grey-rock BIFF: short, factual, neutral. Safer to send to a coercive co-parent.'. The history card is renamed to 'Advocate Review Log' and the button to '+ Log for advocate' (BiffTab.jsx lines 87-104 and 269-290).

design_issues.screen: Footer Get help for signed-out users
issues: footer-get-help only exists in AppShell (AppFooter). Public pages (/login, /register, /privacy-notice, /calendar, /case-settings) only have GlobalCopyright, which has no Get help link. Signed-out users can reach /help from the portal bottom nav (nav-get-help) and the crisis strip, but not from a footer.

accessibility_failures.issue: No role=dialog, aria-modal or aria-labelledby. When it opens, focus stays on nav-biff behind the overlay. Tab reaches nav-print and nav-get-help behind it, so focus isn't contained. Esc closes it but focus goes to BODY instead of back to nav-biff.
From code review only; I couldn't find its launcher in the browser run. No role=dialog or aria-modal, no Escape handler, and no focus move or containment.

At root font-size 200%, the overlay scrolls sideways (scrollWidth 495 vs 390). The 'SA CoParents' header text is clipped behind cb-quick-exit, and cb-quick-exit sits partly off-screen (right=397 at 390). At 195px CSS width (200% zoom), cb-quick-exit right=229 and the progress bar (div.w-32) and cb-copy overflow. The overlay also has no role=dialog and Esc does not close it.

Submit stays disabled until the form is valid and no inline errors are shown. Inputs have no aria-invalid or aria-describedby and nothing goes to role=alert, so screen-reader users aren't told why they can't submit.
The 'Invalid email or password' message is in an aria-live region, so it is announced (pass). But the inputs are not marked aria-invalid or linked to the message.
No <main> or role=main on either page; every other page checked has one.
The portal home has 2 visible h1s and the Communication Builder view has 3.
Native <input type=date>: there is no visible focus on its 4 tab stops, and it uses the browser's own date picker instead of the app's (shadcn) calendar.

accessibility_failures.route: Portal and BIFF drawer (BiffTab 22, AlignmentHub 58, JourneyShell 20 uses)
accessibility_failures.issue: Fixed-pixel font sizes ignore a 200% root font-size, so the grey-rock chip, presets and labels stay at 9-11px while the rest of the text grows. Browser zoom still scales them.

accessibility_failures.selector: login-show-email-toggle 324x16, login-magic-link-button 170x16, register-add-child 132x20, calendar-home-link 41x20, case-settings-back 55x20, plan-options-back 55x20, grey-rock-toggle-on-btn 56x23, biff-ai-learn-more 81x23
accessibility_failures.issue: Below 24px tall. axe passes them only under the spacing exception; raising them to 24px or more is recommended.

accessibility_passes: axe (wcag2a/aa, 21a/aa, 22aa) found 0 violations on /login, /login with error, /register, /help, /calendar, /case-settings, /plan-options, portal home (guest and parent) and the Communication Builder. lang=en everywhere. The AI notice modal (Radix) has role=dialog, Tab stays inside it, and Esc closes it and returns focus to the textarea. /help, /calendar, /case-settings and /plan-options have a logical tab order, no traps, and nothing overflows at 200% root font, 320px or 195px. Real visible horizontal scroll at 200% was confirmed only in the Communication Builder overlay. Portal home and /register report scrollWidth > clientWidth, but horizontal scrolling is locked (scrollX stays 0) and no element is visibly cut off, so I'm not counting it.
action_items: HIGH: In BiffTab.jsx, remove the reason and safety wording shown when Grey-rock is on: the biff-greyrock-chip title ('Quick Safety Check flagged coercion...'), the subtitle 'Safer to send to a coercive co-parent', and the 'Advocate Review Log' / '+ Log for advocate' labels. Use neutral 'Grey-rock tone on' wording only.

Give DrawerShell (JourneyDrawers.jsx) and GuidedJourneyModal proper dialog behaviour: role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby on the title, move focus in when opened, keep Tab inside, close on Esc and return focus to the button that opened it (Radix Dialog as in AiNoticeModals is easiest).

Communication Builder overlay: fix the header at 200% text and 195px width (let the brand text wrap or shrink, keep cb-quick-exit fully on screen), stop the progress bar and cb-copy from overflowing, and consider adding Esc to close and dialog semantics.
Fix contrast: grey-rock-toggle-on-btn (use amber-700 or darker), the BiffTab 'Scenario Presets' label (slate-400 -> slate-600), and the PasswordStrengthMeter levels 1 and 3 colours.
/register: show inline field errors linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid plus a role=alert summary, or explain why Submit is disabled. Mark the login inputs aria-invalid when sign-in fails.
Wrap the /login and /register content in <main>. Make sure there is only one h1 on portal home and in the Communication Builder.
Replace the native date input on /register with the shadcn date picker and give it a visible focus style.

Optional: add a Get help link to GlobalCopyright so signed-out users see it in the footer on public pages. Raise small targets to at least 24px. Switch the text-[9-11px] classes to rem sizes so they grow with text size.
critical_code_review_comments: case_safety_routes._fresh accepts timestamps up to 5 minutes in the future (abs()). That's fine for clock skew, but it means the replay cache (24h TTL) is the only replay defence; that's OK.
A stale or locked webhook still returns 200 {ok:true}. Fine for idempotency, but SACOparentsAlign can't tell a write was ignored except from the admin daily counts.

service-worker.js precaches '/' as the SPA shell, but NEVER_CACHE only covers HTML navigations to /help. The JS bundle can still render /help offline from the cached shell. Help data comes from the API, which is never cached, so this is acceptable.
GetHelp usePrivacyCover hides the page on window blur. On desktop this blanks the page whenever focus moves to devtools or another window; that is by design but worth knowing.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% of Safety Gate, Get Help and Admin flows pass (1 HIGH wording bug); accessibility: 13 findings across 3 dialog/reflow areas and several minor ones
